Brief overview of economic implications: deeper cooperation on key issues - including youth mobility, food and drink, and energy - would help drive economic growth in the UK. Economic growth and cooperation on illegal immigration are at the centre of No 10's arguments for selling a closer relationship at and beyond the upcoming EU summit. Post-Brexit divergence in food standards caused problems for UK food exports to the EU; renegotiating common rules reduced red tape and led to a May 2025 deal granting continued EU fishing-boat access to UK waters until 2038 in exchange for reduced checks on UK food exports, allowing raw burgers and sausages to be sold into the EU for the first time since Brexit. The summit will put further deals on the table covering food and drink, energy trading, and immigration coordination.
